text: Chapter 4 teaches jazz harmonic analysis and chord-tone improvisation through the standard "All of Me," introducing the foundational rule that chord function depends on surrounding chords, and the key concept of secondary dominants -- dominant 7th chords that tonicize scale degrees other than the tonic. The chapter establishes load-bearing terminology including chord tones (the Root, 3rd, 5th, and 7th that structure a chord), provides five complete 7th chord formulas (major 7, dominant 7, minor 7, half-diminished, and diminished 7), and defines chromatic approach notes as decorative rather than structural. Greenan's characteristic pedagogical moves appear in the chord-tone arpeggio exercise, which enforces voice leading by moving to the nearest chord tone of the next chord while maintaining root-3-5-7 order regardless of starting position, and in the color-coded key-center system that tracks harmonic movement across tonal regions. The chapter emphasizes the governing improv philosophy that guide tones (3rds and 7ths) and full chord tones take priority over scales, and includes specific avoidance rules like cautioning against major 3rds or 7ths over iv minor chords.
